reason: Wrong side of the market: BusPlanner is a 40-year-old student-transportation SOFTWARE VENDOR selling routing/GPS/dispatch to the largest PUBLIC school districts in North America (busplanner.com/company/about cites Miami-Dade 300,000+, Gwinnett County 180,000+, Toronto DSB 230,000+ students) — it is precisely the kind of third-party vendor Kenneth Thomas would govern on a school's behalf, not a tuition-funded independent or charter school of 800-2,000 students with a board that cannot answer technology-risk questions. The only matched job, 'Hardware Operations Specialist', is a vendor-side deployment and logistics role owning how GPS/tablet/camera hardware 'gets ordered, installed, trained, supported, and grown' for its own customers; its existence signals BusPlanner's hardware business is scaling, not that an ungoverned school has outgrown reactive outsourced IT. No live posting redescribes the governance gap, the enrollment-attrition EDP, or the legacy-PBX-to-Teams-Phone pain, so there is no qualifying quotable line.
